sentences.text: The patient is a 51-year-old male, and the records contain 10 source reports dated 1990-11-03 to 2021-03-06.
Your records list the following ongoing conditions: chronic sinusitis, diabetes, anemia, hypertension, hyperglycemia, hypertriglyceridemia, metabolic syndrome X, and prediabetes.
For LDL cholesterol (often called 'bad' cholesterol), the latest value was 144.5 mg/dL on 2021-03-06 (usual range below 100 mg/dL), which is above the usual range.
LDL cholesterol changed between Feb 2019 and Mar 2021 as follows: went up from 71.5 to 141.4 and then 144.5 mg/dL.
For HbA1c (average blood sugar over the last few months), the latest value was 7 % on 2021-03-06 (usual range 4-5.6 %), which is above the usual range.
HbA1c changed between Feb 2019 and Mar 2021 as follows: went up from 6.5 to 6.8 and then 7 %.
For triglycerides (a type of blood fat), the latest value was 193.8 mg/dL on 2021-03-06 (usual range below 150 mg/dL), which is above the usual range.
Triglycerides changed between Feb 2019 and Mar 2021 as follows: went up from 108.5 to 197.8 and then 193.8 mg/dL.
For total cholesterol, the latest value was 231.5 mg/dL on 2021-03-06 (usual range below 200 mg/dL), which is above the usual range.
Total cholesterol changed between Feb 2019 and Mar 2021 as follows: went up from 169.4 to 233.2 and then 231.5 mg/dL.
For creatinine (a kidney test), the latest value was 1.3 mg/dL on 2021-03-06 (usual range 0.6-1.2 mg/dL), which is above the usual range.
Creatinine changed between Feb 2019 and Mar 2021 as follows: stayed at 1.2, then stayed at 1.2, and then went up to 1.3 mg/dL.
For blood sugar (glucose), the latest value was 101.6 mg/dL on 2021-03-06 (usual range 70-99 mg/dL), which is above the usual range.
Blood sugar changed between Feb 2019 and Mar 2021 as follows: went up from 84.4 to 105.9 and then down to 101.6 mg/dL.
The other test results did not raise an alert.
Blood pressure was raised on two different days: 145/101 on 2021-03-06 and 194/100 on 2020-02-29.
The haemoglobin result was 15.6 g/dL, which is at or above 13 g/dL.
Your ongoing medicines are amLODIPine 2.5 MG Oral Tablet, 24 HR Metformin hydrochloride 500 MG Extended Release Oral Tablet, and Hydrochlorothiazide 25 MG Oral Tablet.
No allergies are recorded in the supplied records.

sections.title: Points to discuss with your doctor

sentences.text: You might want to talk about your recent blood sugar and cholesterol levels, and your blood pressure readings.
